figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Identification of PcUGTs required for the biosynthesis of anthraquinone glucosides in P. cuspidatum. (a) Phylogenetic tree among
PcUGTs, AtUGTs, and UGTs from various species. Phylogenetic tree was constructed by MEGA X software based on neighbor-joining and 1000
bootstrap replicates. The different groups (A−N) of UGTs are indicated in different colors. The amino acid sequences of respective protein are
listed in Table S2. PcUGTs are highlighted in gray and marked by circles. (b) Content of emodin 6-O-glucoside (E6G) and emodin 8-O-glucoside
(E8G) in the different tissues of P. cuspidatum. Different color for root, stem, and leaf. Letters (a−c) represent significant difference (p < 0.05). (c)
Expression profiles of PcUGT genes in the root, stem, and leaf of P. cuspidatum. Magenta color for high abundance, and blue color for low
abundance. Red dotted box means interested PcUGT genes. (d) Sequence alignment of four PcUGTs was carried out by BioEdit software. Black
marker indicates the same sequence among the four PcUGTs. Magenta dotted box indicates the PSPG domain.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Enzymatic activity of the recombinant proteins GST-PcUGT1, GST-PcUGT73BF6 (PcUGT2), GST-PcUGT95D10 (PcUGT3), and
GST-PcUGT4. The different color curves refer to chromatograms of the enzyme reaction with various substrates, and UDP-Glc as the sugar donor.
PcUGT2 and PcUGT3 are respectively designated as PcUGT73BF6 and PcUGT95D10. (a) Emodin (Emo, 254 nm), (b) resveratrol (Res, 306
nm), (c) quercetin (Que, 360 nm), (d) kaempferol (Kae, 360 nm), (e) naringenin (Nar, 290 nm), and (f) apigenin (Api, 335 nm). The enzymatic
products are as following: Emo 6-O-glucoside (E6G), polydatin (Pol), Que 7-O-glucoside (Q7G), Que 3-O-glucoside (Q3G), Que 4’-O-glucoside
(Q4’G), Kae 7-O-glucoside (K7G), Kae 3-O-glucoside (K3G), Nar 7-O-glucoside (N7G), and Api 7-O-glucoside (A7G).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Functional identification of PcUGT73BF6 in P. cuspidatum and tobacco. (a) Red fluorescences are detected from transgenic hairy roots
of P. cuspidatum. (b) Relative expression level of PcUGT73BF6 in the transgenic hairy roots of P. cuspidatum. Error bars are based on the standard
deviation of three replicates per sample. Letters (a−c) represent significant difference (p < 0.05). (c) Content of E6G in the transgenic hairy roots
of P. cuspidatum. (d) Red fluorescences are observed in tobacco leaves. Green circles indicate obvious red fluorescences. (e−f) The expression of
PcUGT73BF6 in transgenic tobacco leaves. (g) Content of E6G in the transgenic tobacco leaves.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Enzymatic activity of PcUGT73BF6 for various sugar donors. (a) Chemical structures of the six UDP-sugars (UDP-Glc, UDP-Xyl, UDP-
Gal, UDP-GlcA, UDP-Rha, and UDP-Ara). (b) Conversion rate of PcUGT73BF6 toward Emo using diverse UDP-sugars. (c) The formation of
Emo O-rhamnoside (E6R) by PcUGT73BF6 using Emo as the substrate and UDP-Rha as the sugar donor. (d) Mass spectrometric analysis of the
standard E6R. (e) Mass spectrometric analysis of glycosylated product of PcUGT73BF6 for Emo using UDP-Rha as the sugar donor. The
enzymatic product was confirmed by comparing with reference standard.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Mechanism of sugar donor selectivity of PcUGT73BF6. (a) Overall structure model of PcUGT73BF6 docked with Emo and UDP-Glc.
Cyan stick model means the substrate, Emo. Green stick model means the sugar donor, UDP-Glc. Red dashed circle indicates the flexible loop
domain. (b) Sequence alignment between PcUGT73BF6 and glycosyltransferases with favoring for UDP-Rha (RhaGT) and UDP-Xyl (XylGT).
Two residues in the flexible loop are within the red dashed rectangle. (c) Conversion rate of the PcUGT73BF6 mutants using Emo as the substrate
and UDP-Glc, UDP-Xyl, or UDP-Rha as the sugar donor. (d) The cross-section of the substrate binding pocket of PcUGT73BF6 with UDP-Glc
inside. (e,f) The cross-section of the substrate binding pocket of mutant G148S with UDP-Glc (e) or UDP-Xyl (f) inside. (g,h) Interactions
between mutant G148S and UDP-Glc (g) or UDP-Xyl (h). The hydrogen bonds are marked by yellow dashed lines.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. Site-directed mutagenesis of PcUGT73BF6 for improving the catalytic activity for Emo. (a) Interactions between PcUGT73BF6 and
Emo. The hydrogen bonds are marked by yellow dashed lines. (b) Conversion rate of the mutants of amino acids around binding pocket in
PcUGT73BF6 toward Emo using UDP-Glc as the sugar donor. (c) The sugar donor UDP-Glc is bound within the binding pocket of
PcUGT73BF6. Green stick means the sugar donor UDP-Glc. (d,e) Conversion rate (d) and HPLC chromatogram (e) of the PcUGT73BF6
mutants toward Emo using UDP-Glc as the sugar donor. (f,g) Conversion rate (f) and HPLC chromatogram (g) of the PcUGT73BF6 mutants
toward Emo using UDP-Xyl as the sugar donor. Error bars are based on the standard deviation of three replicates per sample.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 7. Mechanism analysis of the improvement of catalytic efficiency for Emo. (a,b) The substrate Emo is bound within the binding pocket of
PcUGT73BF6 (a) or mutant S194G/S394G (b). Cyan stick means the substrate Emo. The narrowest distance within the entrance of binding
pocket is shown by a yellow dashed line. (c,d) The distances of sugar acceptor (Emo), catalytic residue (H20), and sugar donor (UDP-Glc,
UDPG) in the PcUGT73BF6 (c) or S194G/S394G (d) complex. (e,f) The dynamic distances of Emo, H20, and UDPG during the 100 ns MD
simulations. (g) The binding free energy of each residue in the PcUGT73BF6 and S194G/S394G complex for Emo. The values of the binding free
energies of S194/S394 in PcUGT73BF6 and G194/G394 in the mutant S194G/S394G are marked. Whole protein values of the binding free
energies in PcUGT73BF6 and the mutant S194G/S394G are shown.
